You can count, I assume."|{here} is looking for a second again, and spots you at the door before you can leave.|{here} tosses you the coat as you come in, as if it's been decided.} {The opponent is an upper-year with a terrible moustache.|The opponent bows too low, which is a kind of insult.|{season == "winter": The hall is so cold the wands spark on their own.|The gallery has a dozen spectators and a bookmaker.}} Stand as the second {You count, she wins, she doesn't thank you. On the way out she hands you back your scarf, which you hadn't noticed she'd picked up.|She loses on a technicality and blames the handkerchief. Then she buys you a cider, without a word.|You count; she wins in nine seconds. "Adequate," she says, which from Lyra is a medal.} {Bram makes you recite the rules of seconding before he lets you hold his coat. He wins, and gives you a demerit for dropping the handkerchief early, then rescinds it.|Bram loses and stands very straight. Afterwards, gruffly, "Fair count. Thanks."|Bram wins, and for a moment looks up at the gallery as if for someone who isn't there.} {You count the paces, drop the handkerchief and hold the coat through an hour of shouting. {here} owes you one, and knows it.|You stand on the line through a long, sweaty bout. {here} thanks you warmly afterwards.|You second with the calm of long practice. {here} wins, and claps you on the shoulder like an old comrade.} Offer to referee instead {You referee straight down the middle and call a foul against {here}. The gallery approves. {here} does not.|You referee, fairly, and learn more watching both wands than you would holding a coat. {here} feels a little abandoned.|Your call decides the bout. It's the right call; {here} won't admit it till next week.}
